name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: '1.24'
          cache: true

      - name: Check formatting
        if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'
        run: |
          unformatted=$(gofmt -l .)
          if [ -n "$unformatted" ]; then
            echo "These files need gofmt:"
            echo "$unformatted"
            exit 1
          fi

      - run: go vet ./...
      - run: go test -race ./...
      - run: go build ./...

  build-matrix:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: '1.24'
          cache: true
      - name: Cross compile
        run: |
          for target in linux/amd64 linux/arm64 darwin/amd64 darwin/arm64 windows/amd64; do
            GOOS=${target%/*} GOARCH=${target#*/} CGO_ENABLED=0 \
              go build -trimpath -o /dev/null ./cmd/mixpost
            echo "built $target"
          done

name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags: ['v*']

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  goreleaser:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: '1.24'
          cache: true

      - uses: goreleaser/goreleaser-action@v6
        with:
          version: '~> v2'
          args: release --clean
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # Pushes the Homebrew formula and the Scoop manifest to
          # inovector/homebrew-tap and inovector/scoop-bucket.
          TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

# About Mixpost CLI Your whole social media workflow, one command away. Mixpost CLI brings [Mixpost](https://mixpost.app) to the place you already work. Draft, schedule and review your posts, and read how they performed, without opening a browser tab, on Mixpost Cloud or your own self-hosted Pro or Enterprise instance. It also works beautifully with AI assistants like Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor. Ask for three posts about your new feature scheduled for next week, and your agent can do it end to end. ## Install **macOS and Linux: Homebrew** ```bash brew install inovector/tap/mixpost ``` **macOS and Linux: install script** ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/inovector/mixpost-cli/main/install.sh | sh ``` The script picks the build for your system, verifies its checksum and installs it to `/usr/local/bin`, or to `~/.local/bin` when that is not writable. Set `MIXPOST_VERSION` to install a given release and `MIXPOST_INSTALL_DIR` to choose the directory. **Windows: Scoop** ```powershell scoop bucket add inovector https://github.com/inovector/scoop-bucket scoop install mixpost ``` **Binary release** Download the archive for your platform from the [releases page](https://github.com/inovector/mixpost-cli/releases) and put `mixpost` on your `PATH`. On macOS, prefer Homebrew or the install script: a binary downloaded through a browser is unsigned and Gatekeeper blocks it. **Go** ```bash go install github.com/inovector/mixpost-cli/cmd/mixpost@latest ``` **Docker** Build an image from the repository, for CI jobs that run in containers: ```bash docker build -t mixpost --build-arg VERSION=0.1.0 \ https://github.com/inovector/mixpost-cli.git#v0.1.0 docker run --rm -e MIXPOST_PERSONAL_KEY mixpost post list -w acme ``` **From source** ```bash git clone https://github.com/inovector/mixpost-cli && cd mixpost-cli make build && ./mixpost version ``` ## Update Update the way you installed: | Installed with | Update with | |---|---| | Homebrew | `brew upgrade mixpost` | | Scoop | `scoop update mixpost` | | Install script | run the install script again | | Go | `go install github.com/inovector/mixpost-cli/cmd/mixpost@latest` | Once a day, a command run in a terminal checks for a newer release and, when there is one, prints the command that updates your installation. The check runs alongside the command, and never in CI, in a pipe or with structured output. Set `MIXPOST_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1` to turn it off. ## Quick start Create a personal key: open the user menu of your Mixpost dashboard, click **API**, then **Create a personal key**. The key is shown once, so copy it straight away. Then: ```bash mixpost auth login --personal-key mixpost workspace list # find your workspace UUID mixpost config set workspace mixpost account list mixpost post create --text "Hello from the CLI" --account twitter --now ``` Without a URL, the CLI talks to Mixpost Cloud (`https://cloud.mixpost.app/p`). For a self-hosted instance, pass `--url` with the address you open Mixpost at, including its core path: ```bash mixpost auth login --url https://example.com/mixpost --personal-key ``` A trailing `/api` is stripped, so all of these mean the same thing: ``` example.com/mixpost https://example.com/mixpost https://example.com/mixpost/ https://example.com/mixpost/api ``` `cloud.mixpost.app` becomes `https://cloud.mixpost.app/p`. Any other address without a path is tried with the default `/mixpost` core path first and at the site root second, so an instance with an empty `MIXPOST_CORE_PATH` is found at login too. ## Configuration Settings live in `~/.config/mixpost/config.yml` (0600), one entry per profile: ```yaml current_profile: production profiles: production: url: https://example.com/mixpost personal_key: "..." workspace: 3bbd0951-5b04-432b-b2a0-688588b0720e staging: url: https://staging.example.com/mixpost personal_key: "..." ``` Values resolve as **flag → environment variable → profile**: | Variable | Flag | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `MIXPOST_URL` | `--url` | self-hosted Mixpost address, including the core path (default: Mixpost Cloud) | | `MIXPOST_PERSONAL_KEY` | `--personal-key` | personal key | | `MIXPOST_PROFILE` | `--profile` | profile to use | | `MIXPOST_CONFIG` | none | path to the configuration file | | `MIXPOST_OUTPUT` | `-o`, `--output` | default output format | | `MIXPOST_INSECURE` | `--insecure` | skip TLS verification | | `MIXPOST_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER` | none | do not check for newer releases | Switch instances per command with `--profile staging`, or for a whole session with `mixpost config use staging`. ### The workspace is not an environment variable There is no `MIXPOST_WORKSPACE`, deliberately. The URL and the personal access key say **who you are**; the workspace says **what you operate on**. One key reaches many workspaces, so a resource selector carried in ambient environment state would let the same command line mean different things in different shells: ```bash mixpost post delete --permanent --yes # from which workspace, exactly? ``` A wrong URL or key fails loudly with 404 or 401. A wrong but valid workspace succeeds, against the wrong data. So it comes from the profile, which you write deliberately and can read back with `mixpost config list`, or from an explicit `-w` on the command. `-w` takes a uuid, a workspace name or a numeric id: ```bash mixpost post list -w acme mixpost post list -w 3bbd0951-5b04-432b-b2a0-688588b0720e ``` A name is resolved through `GET /workspaces` once per run; a uuid costs no extra request. ## Output `--output` accepts `table`, `json`, `yaml`, `csv`, `tsv`, `id` and `template`. The default is **`table` on a terminal and `json` everywhere else**, so a command in a pipe or a script always produces machine-readable output without being told to. ```bash mixpost post list # table for a human mixpost post list | jq '.data[].uuid' # json in a pipe mixpost post list -o id | xargs -n1 mixpost post get mixpost post list -o csv --no-headers > posts.csv mixpost post list -o template --template '{{range .data}}{{.uuid}} {{.status}}{{"\n"}}{{end}}' ``` JSON output is the API response passed through untouched, so fields this CLI does not know about still reach you. ## Exit codes ``` 0 success 6 422 validation failed 1 generic failure 7 429 rate limited 2 bad invocation or config 8 5xx server error 3 401 not authenticated 9 network failure or timeout 4 403 forbidden 10 cancelled at a confirmation prompt 5 404 not found ``` When the output format is structured, failures are written to stderr as JSON so an agent can read them the same way it reads data: ```json { "error": { "message": "Validation errors", "status": 422, "exit_code": 6, "errors": { "versions.0.content": ["The content is required."] } } } ``` ## Commands Workspace-scoped. These use the workspace from `-w` or the active profile: ``` mixpost account list|get mixpost post list|get|create|update|schedule|queue|approve|delete mixpost tag list|get|create|update|delete mixpost media list|get|upload|status|update|delete mixpost media folder list|create|update|delete mixpost mention list|get|create|update|delete mixpost analytics summary|account|post|posting-times|best-times ``` Instance-level. No workspace needed: ``` mixpost workspace list # the workspaces your personal key can reach mixpost ping # is Mixpost up and the key valid (self-hosted Pro only) ``` Plus `auth`, `config`, `raw`, `version` and `completion`. Run `mixpost --help` for the flags of any of them. ### Scope This CLI covers the API available in **Mixpost Cloud, Pro and Enterprise**. The Enterprise admin panel under `/api/panel`, covering workspace administration, instance users, subscriptions and receipts, is deliberately not wrapped. Those endpoints are still reachable through the escape hatch if you run Enterprise and use the personal key of an admin: ```bash mixpost raw GET panel/workspaces ``` ### Posts Repeating `--text` builds a thread; `--link` and `--media` line up with the text blocks in the same order. ```bash # draft mixpost post create --text "Draft this for later" --account twitter # scheduled, in an explicit timezone mixpost post create \ --text "Launching today" \ --account twitter --account linkedin \ --at "2026-09-10 15:00" --tz Europe/Chisinau # publish now, with media and a tag that is created if missing mixpost post create --text "Look at this" --media 4,5 \ --account 1 --tag launch --create-tags --now # a thread mixpost post create --text "1/ First" --text "2/ Second" --account twitter --queue # per-provider options mixpost post create --text "Sensitive" --account mastodon \ --option mastodon.sensitive=true \ --option youtube.title="Release notes" ``` `--account` and `--tag` take an id, a uuid, a username, a display name or a provider, and are resolved against the workspace before the post is sent. A time without an offset is read in `--tz` when given, and otherwise in the timezone set in your Mixpost user settings. An RFC 3339 time with an offset names an exact instant and is converted for you. Editing reads the post first and applies the flags on top of it, so changing the text does not clear the accounts, tags or schedule, and the post stays at the same moment: ```bash mixpost post update --text "Corrected text" mixpost post update --at "2026-09-11 09:00" ``` Scheduling and approving can move a post as they go, and give an account a time of its own; accounts without one publish with the post: ```bash mixpost post schedule --at "2026-09-10 15:00" --tz Europe/Chisinau \ --account-at linkedin="2026-09-10 18:00" mixpost post approve --at "2026-09-11 09:00" ``` Before a post is scheduled, queued or approved, it is checked against what each of its platforms requires. A post that falls short fails with exit code 6 and one entry per unmet requirement, keyed `requirements...`. Filters on `post list` run on the server, so they reach the whole workspace: ```bash mixpost post list --status scheduled --account linkedin --all mixpost post list --keyword launch --tag campaign ``` Deleting moves posts to the trash. `--permanent` deletes for good and asks first; add `--yes` to confirm in a script. ```bash mixpost post delete mixpost post delete --permanent --delete-mode app_and_social --yes ``` Full control is always available by handing over the JSON body, which the flags then override: ```bash cat post.json | mixpost post create -f - mixpost post create -f template.json --at "2026-09-10 15:00" ``` ### Media ```bash mixpost media upload photo.jpg # single request mixpost media upload video.mp4 --alt-text "Demo" # chunked when it is large mixpost media upload https://example.com/photo.jpg # the instance downloads it mixpost media upload *.png -o id # ids, ready to pipe ``` Files above `--chunk-threshold` (8 MiB by default) switch to the chunked endpoints automatically: the CLI initiates a session, uploads the parts (three at a time, `--concurrency`), completes it, and aborts the session on the server if anything fails. Remote URLs are polled until the download finishes. Folders organise the library without moving any file. A folder is named by uuid, by name when the name is unique, or by its path from the root: ```bash mixpost media folder create Q4 --parent Brand mixpost media upload banner.png --folder Brand/Q4 mixpost media list --folder Brand/Q4 --type image --sort name mixpost media update --folder root --alt-text "Team photo" mixpost media list --usage unused -o id | xargs mixpost media delete --yes ``` ### Mentions A mention holds the handle a person or brand goes by on each network. A post mentions them with `{{mention:}}`, and every account receives the identity its own network expects: ```bash mixpost mention create --name "Ana Popescu" \ --identity bluesky=ana.bsky.social --provider-id bluesky=did:plc:abcdef123456 \ --identity twitter=anapopescu mixpost mention list # the INSERT column is the text to paste mixpost post create --text "Thanks {{mention:42}}!" --account twitter --account bluesky mixpost mention update --remove-identity twitter ``` ### Analytics ```bash mixpost analytics summary --period last_month mixpost analytics account linkedin --type content --sort-by IMPRESSION_COUNT mixpost analytics post mixpost analytics posting-times --tz Europe/Chisinau mixpost analytics best-times --tz Europe/Chisinau # ready for post create --at ``` The table is a digest; `-o json` returns the full response, charts included. ### Any endpoint `raw` reaches endpoints the CLI does not wrap. The path is relative to `/api` and is prefixed with the workspace, except for instance-level paths such as `ping` and `workspaces`; `--no-workspace` forces that for any other path. ```bash mixpost raw GET posts -q page=2 mixpost raw GET ping mixpost raw POST tags -d '{"name":"launch","hex_color":"#60a5fa"}' mixpost raw GET posts --paginate --limit 100 mixpost raw GET panel/workspaces # Enterprise admin API ``` ## Notes for automation and AI agents - **stdout is data only.** Progress, prompts, warnings and errors go to stderr. - **Formats are stable.** `-o json` returns the API response verbatim; `-o id` prints one identifier per line for `xargs`. - **Exit codes are specific.** Branch on 3/4/5/6 instead of parsing messages. - **`--dry-run` prints the request** (method, URL, headers and body) and performs no writes. Read-only lookups still run, because resolving `-w acme` or `--account twitter` to an id is what makes the printed request accurate. - **Destructive commands ask first.** Without a terminal they refuse rather than assume, so an unattended run must pass `--yes` deliberately. - **Writes are not retried blindly.** Retries cover rate limits, network faults and server errors on idempotent methods; a `POST` is only repeated after a `429`, which means the server did not process it. Tune with `--retries`. - **Pagination is one flag.** `--all` walks every page, `--limit N` stops early. A single request for an agent to see what is available: ```bash mixpost --help && mixpost post --help ``` Mixpost also ships a built-in [MCP server](https://mixpost.app/mcp/). Use it for agents that speak MCP; use this CLI for shell-driven agents, cron and CI, where a binary is cheaper than a protocol. ## Development ```bash make test # unit and end-to-end tests against a mock API make race # the same under the race detector make vet fmt make build make snapshot # full release matrix locally, publishes nothing ``` Layout: ``` cmd/mixpost entry point internal/config profiles on disk, URL normalisation internal/mixpost API client: requests, retries, pagination, uploads internal/output table, JSON, YAML, CSV, TSV, id and template rendering internal/cli cobra commands ``` Shell completion: ```bash mixpost completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_mixpost" mixpost completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/mixpost mixpost completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/mixpost.fish ``` ## License [MIT](LICENSE).

# Build an image of the CLI from source, for CI jobs that run in containers:
#   docker build -t mixpost . && docker run --rm -e MIXPOST_PERSONAL_KEY mixpost version
FROM golang:1.24-alpine AS build

WORKDIR /src
COPY go.mod go.sum ./
RUN go mod download

COPY . .
ARG VERSION=dev
RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath \
    -ldflags "-s -w -X github.com/inovector/mixpost-cli/internal/cli.version=${VERSION}" \
    -o /out/mixpost ./cmd/mixpost

FROM alpine:3.20
RUN apk add --no-cache ca-certificates
COPY --from=build /out/mixpost /usr/local/bin/mixpost
ENTRYPOINT ["mixpost"]

module github.com/inovector/mixpost-cli

go 1.24.0

require (
	github.com/spf13/cobra v1.10.1
	github.com/spf13/pflag v1.0.9
	golang.org/x/term v0.35.0
	gopkg.in/yaml.v3 v3.0.1
)

require (
	github.com/inconshreveable/mousetrap v1.1.0 // indirect
	golang.org/x/sys v0.36.0 // indirect
)

BINARY  := mixpost
PKG     := ./cmd/mixpost
VERSION ?= $(shell git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo dev)
COMMIT  ?= $(shell git rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null)
DATE    ?= $(shell date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
LDFLAGS := -s -w \
	-X github.com/inovector/mixpost-cli/internal/cli.version=$(VERSION) \
	-X github.com/inovector/mixpost-cli/internal/cli.commit=$(COMMIT) \
	-X github.com/inovector/mixpost-cli/internal/cli.date=$(DATE)

.PHONY: all build install test race cover vet fmt tidy clean snapshot completions

all: vet test build

build:
	go build -trimpath -ldflags '$(LDFLAGS)' -o $(BINARY) $(PKG)

install:
	go install -trimpath -ldflags '$(LDFLAGS)' $(PKG)

test:
	go test ./...

race:
	go test -race ./...

cover:
	go test -coverprofile=coverage.out ./...
	go tool cover -func=coverage.out | tail -1

vet:
	go vet ./...

fmt:
	gofmt -l -w .

tidy:
	go mod tidy

clean:
	rm -f $(BINARY) coverage.out
	rm -rf dist completions

# snapshot builds the full release matrix locally without publishing anything.
snapshot:
	goreleaser release --snapshot --clean

completions: build
	mkdir -p completions
	./$(BINARY) completion bash > completions/$(BINARY).bash
	./$(BINARY) completion zsh  > completions/_$(BINARY)
	./$(BINARY) completion fish > completions/$(BINARY).fish

version: 2

project_name: mixpost

before:
  hooks:
    - go mod tidy
    - go test ./...

builds:
  - id: mixpost
    main: ./cmd/mixpost
    binary: mixpost
    env:
      - CGO_ENABLED=0
    flags:
      - -trimpath
    ldflags:
      - -s -w
      - -X github.com/inovector/mixpost-cli/internal/cli.version={{ .Version }}
      - -X github.com/inovector/mixpost-cli/internal/cli.commit={{ .ShortCommit }}
      - -X github.com/inovector/mixpost-cli/internal/cli.date={{ .Date }}
    goos: [linux, darwin, windows]
    goarch: [amd64, arm64, arm]
    goarm: ["7"]
    ignore:
      - goos: darwin
        goarch: arm
      - goos: windows
        goarch: arm

archives:
  - id: default
    formats: [tar.gz]
    format_overrides:
      - goos: windows
        formats: [zip]
    name_template: >-
      {{ .ProjectName }}_{{ .Version }}_{{ .Os }}_{{ .Arch }}{{ with .Arm }}v{{ . }}{{ end }}
    files:
      - README.md
      - LICENSE

checksum:
  name_template: checksums.txt

snapshot:
  version_template: "{{ incpatch .Version }}-next"

changelog:
  sort: asc
  filters:
    exclude:
      - "^docs:"
      - "^test:"
      - "^chore:"

# The tap and the bucket are separate public repositories, written with
# TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN: a token that can push to both, since the workflow's own
# token reaches only this repository.
brews:
  - repository:
      owner: inovector
      name: homebrew-tap
      token: "{{ .Env.TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
    homepage: https://mixpost.app
    description: Command line client for the Mixpost API
    license: MIT
    test: |
      system "#{bin}/mixpost", "version"

scoops:
  - repository:
      owner: inovector
      name: scoop-bucket
      token: "{{ .Env.TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
    homepage: https://mixpost.app
    description: Command line client for the Mixpost API
    license: MIT
